summary:
In order to identify earth trends we must account for various sources of data over time. 

Ideally, trends may be observed visually and not only confirmed by statistical analysis, but also empirical evidence.

In summary to help users become data detectives we believe, utilizing pre-existing tools are the first steps to aggregating data into a seamless  user interface to allow for querying the world at large. 

From this we may begin to have users - not just detectives, but seamless interfaces @ scale. 

Data like the globe is vastly cyclic- focus on simplicity.
details:
NASA worldview and various fate sources therein is a powerful tool and from a first responder perspective we want simplify for any user at scale - not just detectives.

To effectively ensure empirical evidence like statistical analysis indicating rate of change over time can have various methods, but to confirm a true trend significance we need to become capable for longer periods of time and archive data is not the issue.

Understanding data and interpreting it in various temporal resolutions is complicated, but a challenge we believe we have solved; furthermore, for this particular challenge- a referred approach was user prompted by short series of questions but we believe that an dynamic ongoing prompt model is best.

A solution that does both visualization and analysis is our priority; therefore, spatial temporal 4D visualization to allow interactive user query input for dynamic spectral output with respect of time is DRP’s creative solution.

This solution is not something that can be obtained in a sprint and will require further iteration, and we hope to gain long term resources to support this initiative.

Thank you for your review and we welcome any questions or further correspondence to the email on file.
